source: due2-native (closes corpus coverage gap: incomparable frontier)
notes: Authored for due2; no origin result. The first corpus frontier with incomparable alternatives, which workflows §9 #3 (declared preference) waits for. No config.preference is set: its format is still open, so the frontier is listed without preference, in the deterministic order of §6.3 (outstanding-set size, then alt_id). alt_id is a digest, so for equal sizes the expected frontier is compared as a set. Duty bearers are the Manager and Counsel, not the requester: the evidence actor must be the bearer (§5.3), and Pending reports each route with who must act.

expected.why: All four permissions apply and all are pending. viaManager and viaManagerAgain share the outstanding set {managerApproval} and collapse into one alternative (§6.3.1). {managerApproval, legalReview} strictly contains each singleton, so viaBoth is dominated (§6.3.2). The two singletons are incomparable: both are on the frontier, no preference is declared, and neither is preferred.

ev-1 is an approve on the export request by the duty's bearer, the Manager: managerApproval is fulfilled. viaManager is now ready (empty outstanding set), which dominates every pending alternative, so Permit.
The requester approved their own export. managerApproval's bearer is the Manager, so ev-1 is no witness (§5.3); nothing changes from scenario 1.
